problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}4x\,dV
$$

where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 1},
$$

and $D$ is a finite region in $xz$-plane enclosed between the $x$-axis, the $z$-axis, and the curve $z+{x}^{2}=1$ in the first quadrant.

activity_context.topic_title: Triple Integrals Over Type III Regions

examples.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Triple Integral Over a Type III Region
examples.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral

$$
\displaystyle \iiint\limits_R 8xy  \: \mathrm{d}V
$$

where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (x,z) \in D, \: 0 \leq y \leq \sqrt x \right\},
$$

and $D$ is the finite region in $xz$-plane enclosed between the $x$-axis, the line $x=1,$ and the line $z=x$ in the first quadrant.
examples.worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a mixed integral, we obtain

$$
\displaystyle \iiint \limits_{R} 8xy \, \textrm{d}V
=
\iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{0}^{\sqrt{x}} 8xy\: \mathrm{d}y \right ]  \mathrm{d}A.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}8xy\,dy]dA & ={∬}_{D}4x[{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=\sqrt{x}}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}4x(x-0)\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}4{x}^{2}\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

We must now evaluate this double integral over the region $D$ in the $xz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063571/assets/1d102b63c3deb8121ea88cdc994b9410cf28f9c3bb29abc5ea4a14d7e1e7c389.png)

We can evaluate our double integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}4{x}^{2}\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}4{x}^{2}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4{x}^{2}[z]_{z=0}^{z=x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4{x}^{2}(x-0)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[{x}^{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & ={1}^{4}-0 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral

$$
{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}4y\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A
$$

given that the region $D$ in the $xz$-plane is given by

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1-z,\,0\le z\le 1}.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}4y\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A & ={∬}_{D}[2{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2x\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $D$ is a type II region in the $xz$-plane.
Therefore, to evaluate our double integral as a repeated integral over this region, we integrate with respect to $x$ and then with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2x\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-z}2x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1-z}2x\,\text{d}x]\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[{x}^{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=1-z}\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(1-z)^{2}\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(1-2z+{z}^{2})\,\text{d}z \\  & ={[z-{z}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{z}^{3}]}_{z=0}^{z=1} \\  & =(1-1+\frac{1}{3})-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
